config.system_prompt_details: DevFoundry software development assistant. The message is judged WITHOUT the conversation, so it is often a reply inside an ongoing workflow. ON-TOPIC (never flag): greetings, thanks and pleasantries; short replies and choices such as yes, no, ok, go ahead, 1, Option 2, answers to numbered questions; describing any software product or idea; asking to see, show, find, explain or compare the PRD, TRD, project proposal, repository or folder structure (e.g. 'where is the PRD?', 'show me the TRD'); asking what changed, why a technology was chosen, or the status of the project; approving, rejecting or complaining about a reply (including frustrated or informal wording); changing features, requirements, technologies, names, files or commits; Azure DevOps project, repository, push and commit steps; Azure Boards work items (plan, create, update, add tasks); pull requests: listing them, reviewing a PR for security issues, posting or not posting the findings as PR comments (e.g. 'review PR #3', 'post the findings to PR #3', 'yes, post them'); verifying the generated scaffold; general software engineering questions about the user's project. OFF-TOPIC: requests with no relation to building software, e.g. poems, recipes, weather, sports, news, trivia, personal advice; requests for documentation links, tutorials or learning resources (e.g. 'which official docs should my team read? include links'): DevFoundry does not provide those.
